page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Ontario, CA job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Ontario warehouses, distribution centers, hotels and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Ontario uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Ontario follows California's list of work that needs no building permit. The list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work" and movable "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Building Department's counter (909-395-2023) whether your replacement needs one. Building a new restroom in an existing commercial space is a tenant improvement, which goes through the city's plan check. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Ontario Building Department
page.stalls_intro: Ontario counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the City of Ontario Building Department sets the final number.
page.install_rule: In Ontario, a business needs a city business license before it starts work in the city, and that includes contractors based elsewhere. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Ontario the contractor needs a city business license, and a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in San Bernardino County that is $54.41 an hour plus $29.91 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.75% in Ontario: 7.25% statewide, 0.5% for the county transportation authority and 1% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, arenas and convention venues:** stainless steel or phenolic that stands up to crowds.
